10|## [0.1.5] - 2026-08-05 (In Progress)

12|### Complete K-Family Conformance (8/8 Passing) ✅
13|
14|**Major milestone**: All quantization types now pass conformance testing with byte-exact match within tolerance.
15|
16|#### Bug Fixes
17|
18|- **Optional output layer detection** (`pesti-conformance/src/lib.rs`)
19|  - Made `output.weight` optional to handle models trained without LM head
20|  - Handles Q2_K, Q3_K quantizations that omit the final linear layer

24|  - Fixed shift overflow when extracting 16 nibbles from single u32
25|  - Split `qs` into two separate u32 values: `qs_low` (bytes 4-7) and `qs_high` (bytes 8-11)
26|  - Prevents 60-bit shifts on 32-bit integers (max valid shift is 31 bits)

33|- **Q6_K dequantization logic** (`pesti-runner/src/gguf_weight_loader.rs`)

35|  - Corrected nibble extraction with left-shift logic

56|### GPU Softmax with Feature Gating 🆕
57|
58|**New capability**: Optional CUDA-accelerated softmax computation for attention kernels.
59|
60|#### Implementation Details
61|
62|- **`pesti-runner/src/kernel/softmax.rs`** - Core softmax implementation
63|  - `CpuSoftmaxKernel`: Numerically stable CPU softmax (max subtraction)
64|  - `CudaSoftmaxKernel`: GPU backend via cudarc (feature-gated)
65|  - `SoftmaxKernel` trait: Abstracts over backends
66|  - `SoftmaxKernelBuilder`: Factory for automatic backend selection
67|
68|- **Feature gating**: Entire module behind `#[cfg(feature = "cuda")]`
69|  - CPU-only builds: Only softmax CPU implementation compiled in
70|  - CUDA builds: Both backends available, builder chooses automatically

74|  - Uses softmax kernel for scores normalization step
75|  - Maintains clean abstraction layer
76|  - Enables future fused GPU kernels without API changes
77|
78|#### Engineering Decisions
79|
80|- **Numerical stability**: Max subtraction prevents overflow for large logits (e.g., [1000, 1001, 1002])
81|- **Optional feature**: Keeps codebase buildable without CUDA dependencies
82|- **Extensible**: Trait abstraction allows easy addition of ROCm, etc.
83|- **Tested**: Unit tests verify CPU implementation correctness

97|#### EDR-001: Consumer GPU Architecture Choice (Ada Lovelace vs Blackwell)
98|**Date**: 2026-08-03  
99|**Status**: ✅ Implemented - Option A selected
100|
101|**Context**: RTX 4070 Ti SUPER (sm_8.9 Ada Lovelace) vs RTX 5060 Ti/5090 (sm_12.0 Consumer Blackwell)
102|
103|**Decision Tree**:
104|- **WGMMA instructions**: Available on BOTH sm_8.9 and sm_12.0 (not just Blackwell!)
105|- **tcgen05 instructions**: Datacenter Blackwell sm_100a only (H100/B200) - NOT consumer GPUs
106|- **mma.sync**: Classic tensor cores - works on ALL Ada Lovelace and Blackwell consumer GPUs
107|
108|**Key Insight**: The WGMMA PTX file targeted `sm_120` (Blackwell), but Ada Lovelace sm_8.9 can run most WGMMA code thanks to backward compatibility!
109|
110|**Options Evaluated**:
111|- **Option A: GEMM-based attention** - Uses existing `CudaGemmKernel` with mma.sync
112|  - ✅ Works on RTX 4070 Ti SUPER right now
113|  - ✅ Leverages verified CUTLASS integration
114|  - ✅ Simple to implement (Q @ K^T via GEMM, softmax CPU, S @ V via GEMM)
115|  - ⚠️ 2 GEMM calls instead of 1 fused kernel
116|  - Expected: 50-100x faster than CPU for attention
117|- **Option B: Dedicated WGMMA/tcgen05 attention** - Custom PTX kernel with fused softmax
118|  - 🚀 Maximum performance for long sequences (4096+ tokens)
119|  - ❌ Requires datacenter GPUs (sm_100a Blackwell/Hopper)
120|  - ❌ Complex to implement and debug
121|  - Keep as future optimization if/when we get B200/H100
122|
123|**Final Decision**: **Option A (GEMM-based attention)** implemented in `GemmBasedAttentionKernel`
124|- Works NOW on consumer GPUs with mma.sync tensor cores
125|- Proven path via llama.cpp (~6-8 tok/s on RTX 4070 Ti SUPER)
126|- Can optimize later if sequence lengths > 4096 become common
127|
128|**Files**: `pesti-runner/src/kernel/attention.rs`, `docs/GPU-ATTENTION-STRATEGY.md`

134|**Status**: ✅ Implemented - cudarc + CUTLASS selected

**Portable Execution Substrate for Transformer Inference**

A learning scaffold for understanding LLM inference internals. Not a product, not a competitor—just my way of climbing onto the real codebase later.

## Why This Exists

Most LLM inference engines (llama.cpp, candle, burn) are **production-ready** but hard to learn from if you're new to:
- GGUF binary format internals
- GPU tensor core kernels (WGMMA, tcgen05)
- Quantization math (Q4_K, Q5_K, Q8_K dequantization)
- Attention kernel optimization

PESTI gives you:

✅ **Learning-first design** - Every component documented with "why" not just "how"  
✅ **Progressive complexity** - CPU → GEMM proxy → fused kernels  
✅ **Honest roadmap** - No benchmark chasing, just understanding  
✅ **Feature-gated builds** - Compile without CUDA for pure Rust learning  

## What's Inside

### Phase 1: Foundations ✅
- **[pesti-gguf](https://crates.io/crates/pesti-gguf)** - Full K-family quantization support (external crate)
- **CPU inference engine** (`pesti-runner`) - Pure Rust transformer primitives
- **Conformance testing** - Byte-exact dequantization verification

### Phase 2: GPU Integration 🆕 (Working via GEMM Proxy)
- **CUTLASS integration** via `cudarc` - Battle-tested NVIDIA kernels
- **GEMM-based attention** - Q @ K^T → softmax → S @ V
- **GPU softmax kernel** - Optional CUDA acceleration with feature gating
- **End-to-end verification** - Real GGUF model inference
